questions.question: The Contingency Fund of India is to be augmented from Rs. 500 crores to _________ crores through the Finance Bill as per the Union Budget 2021-22.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 30,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the union budget of India 2021-22, a proposal to **enhance the Contingency Fund of India from ₹500 crore to ₹30,000 crores was introduced through a Finance Bill**. 
 
• The government has also altered the spending norms of the Contingency Fund of India.
 
• An amount equivalent to **40% of the Fund corpus shall be placed at the disposal of the Secretary, Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure **for the** purpose of meeting unforeseen expenditures like natural disasters and other emergencies**.
 
• The remaining Contingency Fund releases exceeding the given limit** shall be made with the approval of the Secretary to the Government of India, Department of Economic Affairs, after the approval of the Secretary to the Government of India, Department of Expenditure**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The contingency fund was made to tackle **unnatural conditions like disasters and other unforeseen emergency expenses**.
 
• The fund is held by the **Department of Economic Affairs on behalf of the President of India and it can be operated by executive action**.
 
• The fund can be increased through a Finance Bill when Parliament is in session or through an ordinance if the house is not in session.
 
• The Contingency Fund of India is **established under Article 267(1) of the Indian Constitution under the Contingency Fund Of India Act 1950.**

questions.question: When was the Tenth Session of the Constituent Assembly held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6-17 October 1949**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Tenth Session of the Constituent Assembly was held from 6-17 October 1949.
 
• There was a total of 11 sessions of the Constituent Assembly.
 
• The last session of the Constituent Assembly was held from 24 to 26 November and on 26 Constitution of India (with 395 articles, 8 schedules, and 22 parts) was signed and accepted by all.
 
• The Assembly met once again on 24 January 1950, when the members appended their signatures to the Constitution of India but it was not a proper session.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The idea of a constituent assembly was first proposed in 1934 by M.N. Roy.
 
• The Assembly first met on 9 December 1946 but was boycotted by Muslim League.
 
• Under the Cabinet Mission plan of 1946, elections were held for the formation of the constituent assembly
 
• The Constitution of India was drafted by the Constituent Assembly.
 
• It was implemented under the Cabinet Mission Plan on 16 May 1946.
 
• The total time taken to form our constitution was 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days.
 
• And the money spent on framing the constitution: was Rs.64 lakhs.
 
• As our constitution was completed and accepted on the 26 of November 1949.
 
• We celebrate it as Consitution Day.

questions.question: Which of the following is a property of Beryllium?

options.text: Has a low melting and boiling point

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Forms covalent compounds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Beryllium **is a **silvery-white metal** which is relatively **soft **and has a **low density.**
 
• Beryllium is used in gears and cogs, particularly in the aviation industry.
 
• It has a very **high melting point making it useful in nuclear work as well as having ceramic applications**.
 
• Beryllium is used as an **alloying agent in the production of beryllium copper.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Beryllium and its compounds are** toxic and carcinogenic** which makes it unsuitable for humans.
 
• The beryllium content on** Earth's crust is 2.6 ppm and in soil 6 ppm**.
 
• **Beryllium **is the only alkaline earth metal that does not react with water because the **size of beryllium is small and the ionization energy of this alkaline earth metal is high when compared to other elements in the group**.

questions.question: Acceleration is equal to the rate of change of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **velocity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Velocity/ speed: The rate of change of displacement/distance of a body is called the velocity/speed of that body.

 
 
• Velocity is a vector quantity that has both magnitudes as well as direction.
 
 
 
• Acceleration: The rate of change of velocity is called the acceleration of the body.
 
 
• Acceleration is also a vector quantity.
 
 
 
• The slope of any velocity-time graph gives an acceleration of the body.
 
• Displacement: The minimum path length between two points is called displacement.
 
• Distance: The total path length between two points is called distance.

Explanation:__

From the above explanation, we can see that, 

__
 
• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity
 
• In other words, it is the ratio of change in velocity and time taken
 
• It has SI units of m/s2 and is also the derivative of velocity

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __Description__

questions.question: Acidic drain cleaners made of ________ or ________ acid are powerful enough to clear heavy-duty hair, food, grease, soap scum, or paper-based clogs in 15 minutes or less.

• **Acid drain cleaners** commonly contain a **high concentration **of** sulfuric acid(H₂SO₄) or hydrochloric (HCL) acid,** and typically come in** liquid form**.
 
• They work by a process of acid hydrolysis to dissolve the fats and solids that create a drain blockage.
 
• Acid hydrolysis is the process of breaking down larger molecules into smaller molecules by adding acid and water to a substance.
 
• They work well on hair and grease, and they can dissolve small pieces of paper and other solids in the drain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Who among the following was an ancient Indian mathematician-astronomer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Varahamihira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Varahamihira**, also known as Varaha or Mihira, **was an Indian philosopher, astronomer, and mathematician**. 
 
• He was born in** 505 A.D. in a Brahmin family at Kapittha, a village near Ujjain**.
 
• He **proposed that the Moon and planets are lustrous not because of their own light but due to sunlight**.
 
• He was one of the **nine gems of the court of **legendary ruler **Yashodharman Vikramaditya of Malwa**.
 
• Varahamihira’s main work is the book **Pancha Siddhantika **(Treatise on the five Astronomical Canons gives us information about older Indian texts which are now lost).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• His important works also include** Brahma Samhita** which covers wide-ranging subjects of human interest, including astrology, planetary movements, eclipses, rainfall, rainfall, clouds even domestic relations, gems, pearls, and rituals.
 
• Varahamihira’s mathematical work included** the discovery of trigonometric formulas**.
 
• He was inspired by the great mathematician and astrologer of India **Aryabhatta**.
 
 
• **Nagarjuna- Indian Buddhist Philosopher**
 
• **Banabhatta- Sanskrit prose writer and poet of India**
 
• **Amalananda- Sanskrit Scholar**

questions.question: Which of the following statements about ‘Swachh Survekshan - Urban’ is INCORRECT?

• Swachh Survekshan - Urban is conducted by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**.
 
• It was** introduced by MoHUA in 2016** as a competitive framework to encourage cities to improve the **status of urban sanitation while encouraging large-scale citizen participation**.
 
• It is the world's** largest urban sanitation and cleanliness survey**.
 
• It was first conducted in** 2016 in 73 cities **having a population of one million or more and the capital city of States/ UTs and Mysore had bagged the award of being the cleanest city in India.**​**

•

questions.question: Which of the following Mauryan rulers did Seleucus fight against in the Seleucid–Mauryan War?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta Maurya**__.

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya fought against Seleucus in the Seleucid-Maurya War**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• ​In 305 BCE, Emperor Chandragupta Maurya led a series of campaigns to retake the satrapies left behind by Alexander the Great when he returned westward.
 
• Seleucus I fought to defend these territories, but both sides made peace in 303 BCE.
 
• Seleucus lost the Seleucid-Mauryan War, and the two rulers reconciled with a peace treaty. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• In 305 BCE, Seleucus I tried to reconquer the northwestern parts of India in order to claim them for the growing Seleucid Empire.
 
• Little is known of the campaign in which Chandragupta fought with Seleucus over the Indus Valley and the region of Gandhara—a very wealthy kingdom that had submitted decades earlier to Alexander the Great.
 
• The Greeks offered a Macedonian princess for marriage to Chandragupta, and several territories, including the satrapies of Paropamisade (modern-day Kamboja and Gandhara), Arachosia (modern-day Kandahar), and Gedrosia (modern-day Balochistan). 
 
• In return, Chandragupta sent 500 war elephants, a military asset that would play a decisive role in Seleucus’ victory against western Hellenistic kings at the Battle of Ipsus in 301 BCE.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India amended Article 19 and inserted provisions fully securing the constitutional validity of zamindari abolition laws in general and certain specified State Acts in particular?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First Amendment**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first amendment of** **the **Indian Constitution was done in 1951**.
 
• Constitution (**First Amendment) Act, 1951 amended Articles 15, 19, 85, 87, 174, 176, 341, 342, 372 and 376.**
 
• Nehru administration made a** provision limiting Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution of India against "abuse of freedom of speech and expression.**
 
• ​The** right of citizens of India to practice any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade, or business conferred by article 19(1)(g)** is subject to reasonable restrictions that the laws of the State may impose, in the interests of the general public.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• There is a total of **106 amendments **made in the Indian constitution, till now.
 
• The provision for amendments is given in **article 368 of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• **Dr . Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar** is known as the father of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **42nd amendment** is also known as** the mini-constitution of India**.
 
• Amendments in our I**ndian constitution are adopted** from the constitution of **South Africa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Which amendment to the Constitution of India added a new subject in the Union List called 'taxes on services’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**88th**.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The division of powers between the Union and the States is in the Seventh Schedule.
 
• Seventh Schedule
 
• It contains three lists:
 
 
• Union List,
 
• State List and
 
• Concurrent List
 
 
 
• 7th Schedule of Indian Constitution – Union List had 97 subjects.
 
• Now, it has 100 subjects.
 
 
• 88th Amendment added a new subject in the Union List called ‘taxes on services.’
 
 
 
• The state list has 61 subjects. Earlier, it had 66 items.
 
 
• The 69th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1991 made special provisions in relation to National Capital.
 
• Laws cannot be made by the Delhi government on three subjects under State List named as – Public Order, Police & Land.
 
 
 
• The concurrent list has 52 subjects enumerated under it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• 85th Amendment:

 
 
• Reservation in promotion for Scheduled Caste tribe candidates in government services.
 
 
 
• 87th Amendment: 
 
 
• ​Extend the usage of 2001 national census population figures for statewide distribution of parliamentary seats.
 
 
 
• 88th Amendment (2003):
 
 
• ​Provision of tax on services.
 
 
 
• 91st Amendment (2003) :
 
 
• Amendment in party change system, recognition of merger of an entire party only.
 
 
 
• 56th Amendment:
 
 
• 56nd Amendment Act, 1987 of the Indian Constitution conferred Statehood on Goa and forms a new Union Territory of Daman and Diu.
 
• Goa thus became the 25th State of the Indian Republic.
 
 
 
• 62nd Amendment:
 
 
• The 62nd Amendment Act extends by 10 years the reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies as well as nomination representatives of the Anglo-Indian community.

questions.question: _________ develops on crystalline igneous rocks in areas of low rainfall in the eastern and southern part of the Deccan Plateau.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red Soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Red soil develops on crystalline igneous rocks in areas of low rainfall in the **eastern and southern parts of the Deccan Plateau and also along the piedmont zone of the western ghats**.
 
• The **soil develops a reddish color due to a wide diffusion of iron in crystalline and metamorphic rocks**.
 
• Red soils denote the** largest soil group of India, covering an area of about 350,000 sq. km (10.6% of India's area) across the Peninsula**.
 
• It contains **thin organic and organic-mineral layers of highly leached soil** resting on a red layer of alluvium.
 
• The red soils, with the proper use of fertilizers and irrigation techniques, give a good yield of **cotton, wheat, rice, pulses, millets, tobacco, oil seeds, potatoes, and fruits**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Approximately 10.6% of the total geographical area of India is covered by **red soil,** including

 
 
• **​****Tamil Nadu, parts of Karnataka, southeastern Maharashtra, eastern Andhra Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh, Orissa, Chhattisgarh, Chota Nagpur (Jharkhand), south Bihar, West Bengal (Birbhum and Bankura), Uttar Pradesh (Mirzapur, Jhansi, Banda, and Hamirpur), Aravallis, eastern Rajasthan, Assam, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, and Meghalaya**
 
 
 
• **Alluvial Soil:**
 
 
• **​**Mostly available soil in India (about 43%) covers an area of 143 sq. km, **wheat, maize, sugarcane, pulses, oilseed, etc. are mainly cultivated.**
 
 
 
• **Arid Soil:**
 
 
• **​**Also known as **Desert soil**, it accounts for over 4.42 % of the total land area of the country. 
 
• These soils are saline in nature and in certain regions the salt content is so high that common salt is obtained by evaporating water.
 
 
 
• **Black Soil:**
 
 
• **​**Black soil is also known as **“Regur Soil” or the “Black Cotton Soil”.**
